mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1500 thousand units consistently precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to accelerated consumer spending and business investment momentum.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return distribution in periods of rising HOUST (3-month increase > 0.5%) shows no significant positive skew compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% for two consecutive months, it triggers aggressive monetary tightening expectations that compress equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for 2+ months, the 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 3-month increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals labor market strength that fuels consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to produce positive 60-day returns in > 40% of instances (60-day returns negative in > 40% of cases) or Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 4Q-4Q growth > 2.5% annualized), a 3-month decline in GDP growth momentum (GDPC1 3-month change < 0.5%) triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to premature policy tightening fears.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns in periods where GDPC1 4Q-4Q growth rate > 2.5% are positive in > 60% of cases (signal fails to predict negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation exceeds 3.5% for two consecutive months, it activates aggressive central bank response expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods of CPIAUCSL YoY inflation > 3.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of cases (Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent 3-month rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust economic activity that drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising INDPRO and RSAFS fails to produce positive 60-day returns in > 40% of instances (60-day returns negative in > 40% of cases) or Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month decline in unemployment (UNRATE) above 3.0% consistently correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved labor market conditions and consumer spending.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return distribution in periods of declining UNRATE (6-month decrease > 0.2%) shows no significant positive skew compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In post-recession recovery phases (HOUST < 1500 thousand units), a 3-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer confidence and spending momentum.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST < 1500, the 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of cases (signal fails to predict negative returns).
